text: A reply shall be classed as a game turn post only if its text has exactly one line matching ^Answers: (none|[a-z2-7]{13}( [a-z2-7]{13})*)$ and exactly one line matching ^Asks: (none|[a-z2-7]{13}( [a-z2-7]{13})*)$.
acceptance: The turn 49 draft as written (modulo-turn49-1111, 'Asks this turn: 0') is classed ordinary with reason 'lines'; the same text with 'Answers: 3n22hvbmous2n' and 'Asks: none' added passes this condition; two Asks: lines fail it.
rationale: No turn post 1-49 carries a machine-readable ask list; prose counts are not a key.

text: A reply shall be classed as a game turn post only if its parent's rkey equals the first rkey on its Answers: line, or, when that line is 'Answers: none', the first rkey on its Asks: line.
acceptance: Turn-49-shaped fixture (Answers: 3n22hvbmous2n, Asks: none, parent 3n22hvbmous2n) passes; turn-48-shaped fixture (Answers: none, Asks: 3n22hvbmous2n) passes; a parent equal to the second Answers rkey fails with 'parent'; both lines none fails with 'parent'.
rationale: Replaces Modulo's GAMECAP-FIRST: turns usually reply under an ask they answer (listed by the previous turn), not one they list (47, 49).

text: A reply shall be classed as a game turn post only if its Answers: line equals the Asks: line of the most recent sent.jsonl entry with game_turn true, the check being skipped when that entry has no Asks: line.
acceptance: Previous game turn 'Asks: a b' and draft 'Answers: a b' passes; draft 'Answers: a' fails with 'chain'; previous entry without an Asks: line skips the check.
rationale: Makes the parent claim checkable from our own log; same check the second key makes under commit-first.

text: When a game turn post is sent, its sent.jsonl line shall carry "game_turn": true, and GAMECAP-CEIL shall measure from the 'at' of the most recent such line.
acceptance: After one game turn post and one ordinary reply, exactly one new sent.jsonl line has game_turn true; a second game turn post 10799 s after the first is held with reason 'ceiling' even though an ordinary reply went out in between.
rationale: The ceiling and the seven-day count need to know which past sends were game turns.
